free_tier.stated: Free hosting with no stated numeric cap. Spotify's own episode-publishing doc: 'We don't have a file size limit'. The video doc repeats it: 'Spotify for Creators doesn't have a file size limit'. No episode count, storage or bandwidth cap is published anywhere — free, no paid tier, ad-revenue share is upside not a paywall.

retention.stated: Second caveat: anchor.fm enclosures are 402/302 chains through anchor.fm/s/<id>/podcast/play/<n>/<urlencoded origin>, so the enclosure URL is a redirector with the object path embedded — permanent, but the served object is always the transcode.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered via Spotify's own CDN (d3ctxlq1ktw2nl.cloudfront.net). No egress meter, no per-download charge, no plan upgrade that changes it.

tooling: No documented public upload API (the old Anchor API is gone; community projects like mahendranv/anchor-rss only scrape the public RSS). Upload is web/mobile UI only. Read side is a permanent RSS at https://anchor.fm/s/<showid>/podcast/rss — plain GET, no auth, serves the full back catalogue (one feed I pulled was 5.2 MB of XML).
chaining: Unlimited shows per Spotify account (the UI has 'Add a new show' with no published cap) x unlimited episodes x no file-size limit. Also accepts video (MP4/MOV/MPG) on the same free tier, so the payload need not be audio at all.
limits_note: Format allowlist is narrow: audio must be MP3, M4A or WAV, mono or stereo; video MOV/MPG/MP4. Uploads are single-shot HTTP from the browser, so a dropped connection mid-upload fails the episode ('higher chance of failing if your internet connection is interrupted') — there is no resumable/chunked API, which is the real ceiling on file size in practice.

reliability_note: RE-ENCODES everything to 128 kbps stereo. Verified live: enclosure for an episode with itunes:duration 00:52:22 declared length=50272965; the staging object at d3ctxlq1ktw2nl.cloudfront.net/staging/2026-9-21/434650861-44100-2-6d67ddd17af0f.mp3 returns 206, Content-Range 0-1023/50272965, and its first 1 KB is a bare MPEG frame with no ID3 header at all. 50,272,965 x 8 / 3142 s = 128,003 bps — exactly 128 kbps CBR. The '-44100-2-' in the filename is the ingest normaliser's fingerprint (44.1 kHz, 2 channels). Your WAV or 320k MP3 does not survive. Second caveat: anchor.fm enclosures are 402/302 chains through anchor.fm/s/<id>/podcast/play/<n>/<urlencoded origin>, so the enclosure URL is a redirector with the object path embedded — permanent, but the served object is always the transcode.
